**Alonzo Harding Mourning Jr.** (born February 8, 1970) is an American former professional [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player who has served as vice president of player programs and development for the [Miami Heat](/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") since June 2009.[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2) Mourning played most of his 15-year [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) career for the Heat.

Nicknamed "**Zo**", Mourning played the [center](/wiki/Center_(basketball) "Center (basketball)") position. Following his college basketball career at [Georgetown University](/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University"), his tenacity on defense twice earned him the [NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award](/wiki/NBA_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award") and twice placed him on the [NBA All-Defensive Team](/wiki/NBA_All-Defensive_Team "NBA All-Defensive Team"). Mourning made a comeback after undergoing a kidney transplant and later won the [2006 NBA championship](/wiki/2006_NBA_Finals "2006 NBA Finals") with the Heat. Mourning also played for the [Charlotte Hornets](/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets") and [New Jersey Nets](/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"). On March 30, 2009, Mourning became the first Miami Heat player to have his number retired.[[3]](#cite_note-Jersey_ESPN-3) In 2010, Mourning was inducted into the [Virginia Sports Hall of Fame](/wiki/Virginia_Sports_Hall_of_Fame "Virginia Sports Hall of Fame"). In August 2014, Mourning was inducted into the [Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame](/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame"), and in August 2019 he was inducted into the [FIBA Hall of Fame](/wiki/FIBA_Hall_of_Fame_member "FIBA Hall of Fame member").

The following table lists the 20 distinct runs as the most-subscribed YouTube channel recorded since May 2006. Only runs lasting at least 24 hours are included. Twelve different channels have held the position, with [PewDiePie](/wiki/PewDiePie "PewDiePie") holding the title a record four times. He also holds the records for the longest time as the most-subscribed channel (1,920 days in his third run), the shortest time as the most-subscribed channel (four days in his second run), and the longest overall combined time as the most subscribed channel (2,017 days). In second place is [Smosh](/wiki/Smosh "Smosh"), which held it three times, while third place is tied between [nigahiga](/wiki/Ryan_Higa#Channels "Ryan Higa"), [T-Series](/wiki/T-Series_(company) "T-Series (company)"), and [YouTube's own channel](/wiki/YouTube_(YouTube_channel) "YouTube (YouTube channel)"), which have all held it twice each. YouTube's own official channel, then known as "YouTube Spotlight", briefly held the title in late 2013; one factor that contributed to the channel's rise to the top spot was the site's autosuggestion for new users to subscribe to the channel upon registration.[[29]](#cite_note-Spotlight-34)

Overall of the twelve channels who have held the record, seven featured individual males (including MrBeast[[D]](#cite_note-mrbeast-brand-35)); one (Brookers) featured an individual female; three have been operated by brands as opposed to individuals (T-Series, YouTube Spotlight, and MrBeast[[D]](#cite_note-mrbeast-brand-35)); one (Smosh) was a duo of males which later became a collective and production company; and one (lonelygirl15) was a web series. Nine of the channels were based in the United States, one (geriatric1927) was based in England, one (T-Series) was based in India, and one (PewDiePie) was based in Sweden, and later in England.

Although the university was incorporated in 1878, it was not until June 20, 1881 that it received the right to confer degrees in arts, divinity and medicine. In 1882, the name of the university was revised to The Western University and College of London, Ontario.[[13]](#cite_note-uwo.ca-14) The first convocation of graduates was held on April 27, 1883.[[11]](#cite_note-not_stated_1889_295-12) Initially affiliated with the [Church of England](/wiki/Church_of_England "Church of England"),[[13]](#cite_note-uwo.ca-14) the university became [non-denominational](/wiki/Non-denominational "Non-denominational") in 1908.

In 1916, the university's current site was purchased from the Kingsmill family. There are two World War I memorial plaques in University College. It consists of an archipelago 80 km (50 mi) south of [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy"), 284 km (176 mi) east of [Tunisia](/wiki/Tunisia "Tunisia"),[[13]](#cite_note-ashby-15) and 333 km (207 mi) north of [Libya](/wiki/Libya "Libya").[[14]](#cite_note-16)[[15]](#cite_note-17) The two official languages are [Maltese](/wiki/Maltese_language "Maltese language") and [English](/wiki/English_language "English language") but Maltese is recognised as the national language.[[16]](#cite_note-18) The country's capital is [Valletta](/wiki/Valletta "Valletta"), which is the [smallest capital city](/wiki/List_of_national_capitals_by_population "List of national capitals by population") in the [European Union](/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) by both area and population.

With a population of about 574,250[[17]](#cite_note-19) spread over an area of 316 km2 (122 sq mi),[[6]](#cite_note-Zammit-6) Malta is the world's [tenth-smallest country by area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area")[[18]](#cite_note-20)[[19]](#cite_note-21) and the [ninth-most densely populated](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density"). Various sources consider the country to consist of a single [urban region](/wiki/Urban_region "Urban region"),[[20]](#cite_note-WUP-22)[[21]](#cite_note-ESPON-EUC-23) for which reason it is often described as a [city-state](/wiki/City-state "City-state").[[22]](#cite_note-GMB_Publishing-24)[[23]](#cite_note-creativemalta-25)[[24]](#cite_note-doi-26)
